body:
Lee and Fein (2000), [DOI 10.1016/S0009-2541(99)00191-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0009-2541(99)00191-6), is a promising microbial complement to the separate abiotic gibbsite dissolution evidence under review in round70.

The title is *Experimental study of the effects of Bacillus subtilis on gibbsite dissolution rates under near-neutral pH and nutrient-poor conditions*. Crossref identity was verified. The publisher XML route returned only metadata (2,045 bytes), and the inspected Fein laboratory publication page did not supply this original. Those observations do not establish that the article is unavailable elsewhere. No microbial measurements or mechanism are accepted from its abstract.

Follow-up acceptance criteria:

- Acquire the complete original through a legitimate publisher or institutional route, retaining origin, access date and checksum. Inspect all relevant figures, tables and any supplements.
- Verify gibbsite preparation, organism/strain provenance, biomass state, media, pH control, replication, sampling and aluminium analytical fractions.
- Compare sterile controls and distinguish dissolution, adsorption/desorption and aqueous accumulation; preserve null or inhibitory results and source inconsistencies.
- Update the existing gibbsite owner only for supported claims, with canonical EDIT history, an independent exact-state scientific review and the standard validation gates. Do not create a duplicate mineral or inherit aluminium criticality.

This is a source-access and scientific-assessment follow-up, not a defect in the bounded abiotic record. Raw acquisition receipts are retained in `/private/tmp/cmm-round70-aluminium-research/`; the round70 source dossier records the search limits. No author contact or access-control bypass was attempted.
title: Acquire Lee and Fein 2000 primary evidence before microbial gibbsite curation
dedup_scope: All137 issues fetched across open/closed states; no matching DOI in title/body. Local hidden/ignored-inclusive source searches recorded separately.
